title: Unfortunate News for Micron Stock and Sandisk Stock Investors | MU Stock | SNDK Stock
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Parkevtate reacts to news that China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has made significant progress on a higher-density memory-cell design, sending Micron, SanDisk, SK Hynix and Samsung down roughly 2–4% (SanDisk about 6%). Drawing on a clip from his October 12 members' Q&A, he explains why he ranks Nvidia above Micron despite Micron's two consecutive quarters of 80%-plus operating margins — a feat he says he has never seen from any company: Nvidia's moat is one to two steps ahead of rivals, whereas Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung are technologically close, so competition was always likely to intensify and could pressure average selling prices even under long-term customer agreements. The industry is sold out through 2026–27 and likely 2028, so any CXMT impact is distant. His calls: MU BUY at $989 stated with fair value $1,400 (about 42% upside), reiterated with no flip — the dip is a buying opportunity with enough margin of safety; SNDK CONDITIONAL_BUY, a first tracked call, with fair value $1,662 implying only about 11–12% upside — fairly valued to slightly undervalued, suitable only for higher-risk-tolerant investors. NVDA and TSM appear as UNCERTAIN comparative mentions, both named among his preferred, more-undervalued options in the category.

calls.bear_case: Price-range clauses in long-term customer agreements could cut ASPs as SK Hynix/Samsung/CXMT competition builds; 80%+ margins invite rivals.
